combat_history.event: Tomahawks opened the air campaign against Iraq, striking heavily defended Baghdad targets without risking aircrew.
combat_history.significance: Established the cruise missile as the standard opening move of U.S. campaigns.

combat_history.event: 59 Tomahawks struck a Syrian airbase in response to a chemical attack.
combat_history.significance: Demonstrated rapid, large-salvo precision strike from destroyers.

combat_history.event: Roughly 66 Tomahawks fired (with allied weapons) against Syrian chemical-weapons sites.
combat_history.significance: Continued reliance on Tomahawk for standoff punishment strikes.

modernization.description: Adds an anti-ship seeker, giving the fleet a long-range surface-strike weapon.
modernization.impact: Closes a long-range anti-ship gap against peer navies.

modernization.description: Army/USMC ground launchers firing Tomahawk and SM-6.
modernization.impact: Puts mobile land-based long-range strike on Indo-Pacific islands.

vulnerabilities.description: At ~880 km/h the missile gives modern IADS time to detect and engage it.
vulnerabilities.context: Against a dense peer air-defence network, attrition can be significant.
vulnerabilities.mitigation: Low-altitude flight, salvo saturation, terrain masking and decoys.

vulnerabilities.description: Navigation accuracy can be degraded by jamming/spoofing.
vulnerabilities.context: Peer adversaries field capable GPS denial.
vulnerabilities.mitigation: TERCOM/DSMAC and anti-jam upgrades in Block V.

operational_patterns.typical_deployment: Salvo land-attack from destroyers, cruisers and submarines at campaign opening; emerging anti-ship and ground-launched roles.
operational_patterns.typical_task_group: Carrier strike groups, surface action groups, SSGNs/SSNs; allied surface combatants.
operational_patterns.readiness_notes: Mass-produced and widely stocked; recapitalised via Block V buys.

peer_comparisons.key_differences: Kalibr is Russia's equivalent ship/sub-launched land-attack cruise missile, used extensively against Ukraine.
peer_comparisons.video_angle: Tomahawk vs Kalibr — the two great-power cruise missiles compared.

peer_comparisons.key_differences: China's land-attack cruise missiles, air- and ground-launched, central to its own standoff strike.
peer_comparisons.video_angle: How the US and China each built their cruise-missile arsenals.

peer_comparisons.key_differences: LRASM is a stealthy air-launched anti-ship missile; Maritime Strike Tomahawk gives ships a longer-ranged surface option.
peer_comparisons.video_angle: America's two answers to the anti-ship problem.

doctrine.role: Long-range precision land-attack (and now anti-ship) cruise missile launched from ships, submarines and ground platforms.
doctrine.employment: Opens campaigns and conducts standoff strikes from beyond defended airspace; ground-launched and allied variants extend conventional deterrence in the Indo-Pacific.
doctrine.design_philosophy: Accuracy, range and mass-producibility over speed — kept decisive by continuous guidance, networking and warhead upgrades.
doctrine.threat_context: Allied proliferation (Japan, Australia, USMC/Army Typhon) is giving the first island chain a conventional counterstrike capability against China.
doctrine.comparison_frame: The Western benchmark cruise missile — read against Russia's Kalibr and China's CJ-10.
